To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

clearance of hepatitis C virus (with DAAs) is not associated with improvements in hemoglobin A _{1c} (HbA _{1c} ), and that total and low-density-lipoprotein cholesterol increase following hepatitis C virus clearance.

clearance of HCV with DAAs was not associated with improvement in HbA _{1c} in patients with and without HIV, and there were no differences in HbA A1c improvement between HIV-infected and noninfected patients.

clearance of hepatitis C with DAAs is not associated with sustained improvements in glycemia, but is associated with increases in total and LDL cholesterol, and that these effects are similar for patients with and without HIV infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of hepatitis C viral clearance with DAAs in the context of HIV.
the effect of directly acting antiviral therapy for hepatitis C infection on hemoglobin A1C and other markers of glycemia.
the effect of hepatitis C treatment with direct acting antivirials (DAA).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HCV clearance with DAAs is not associated with any significant improvement in the glycemic control.
there is no improvement in glycemic control following HCV viral clearance.
there was no improvement in HbA 1c following viral clearance in patients with and without HIV infection, and that the study was not powered to detect a difference in HbAic levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HbA1C and lipid changes following HCV clearance were minimal.
we did not find any improvement in glycemic control following HCV clearance in our patients, irrespective of HIV infection, fibrosis stage, or preexisting diabetes.
there is no evidence that clearance of chronic hepatitis C virus infection with directly acting antvirals is associated with significant changes in glycemia or lipids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are no benefits in glycemia after HCV clearance with DAAs.
HCV clearance is associated with minimal changes in glycemic control and no improvement in glycemia, even in patients with diabetes.
HbA1C does not improve after HCV clearance.
